thesis: Lennox International Inc. (LII) designs, manufactures, and markets energy-efficient heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) equipment for residential and commercial customers. **[Fact]** The company reports two segments: **Home Comfort Solutions** (residential furnaces, air conditioners, heat pumps, indoor air quality) and **Building Climate Solutions** (commercial HVAC, refrigeration, parts distribution). **[Fact]** FY2025 consolidated net sales were **$5,195 million** (down 3% from $5,341 million in 2024), operating income **$1,042 million** (flat), net income **$806 million**, and free cash flow approximately **$639 million** (operating cash flow **$758 million** minus capital spending **$119 million**). **[Fact]** Home Comfort Solutions earned **$728.5 million** segment profit on **$3,343 million** of sales (21.8% margin); Building Climate Solutions earned **$434.2 million** on **$1,852 million** of sales (23.4% margin). Lennox sells through independent dealers, distributors, and national accounts under the Lennox, Armstrong Air, Ducane, and Allied brands.
why_market_wrong: The market may treat Lennox as a peak-cycle HVAC name and underweight its pricing power, buyback discipline, and the offset from Building Climate. **[Fact]** Consolidated gross margin rose 10 basis points to **33.4%** in 2025 despite a **13%** volume decline, as **9%** price and mix partially offset volumes. **[Fact]** The company repurchased **$482 million** of stock in 2025 (versus **$54 million** in 2024) and raised the dividend to **$4.55** per share from **$4.36**. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on Home Comfort volume weakness (sales down **7%** in 2025) and Q1 2026 earnings softness (diluted EPS **$3.35** versus **$3.63** in Q1 2025) and miss that Building Climate grew segment profit **9%** and management is returning capital at scale. At **~$552** per share, however, the stock prices in much of that quality: there is no dated catalyst; the inefficiency is **descriptive** (premium compounder above our return hurdle), not an equity yield curve setup.
